messages:
Cam: heads-up — we're seeing a sudden queue spike on the us-west1 GPU pool, started ~11:12 UTC. ~30% of requests queued >200ms, some tenants getting 429/503 backpressure. Kibana: https://kibana.redwood.example/app/observability#/discover?id=abc123
Maria: seeing alerts too. autoscaler didn't pre-warm additional nodes on that pool? warm_pool_min currently 2.
Cam: confirmed. spike looks like short bursts from a small set of tenants (tenant:acme-prod, tenant:edge-cs). lots of small requests (50-100 tokens) causing many allocations and cache misses -> queueing.
Kev: quick mitigation ideas: increase warm_pool_min to 6 in us-west1, bump scale_up_threshold to 65%, and cap per-tenant RPS (leaky-bucket) to limit intake during spikes.
Maria: +1. I'll apply the warm pool bump and watch latency.
Anya: also recommend raising scale_down_grace to 600s (10m) to avoid flapping after the burst. we saw churn causing additional scheduling lag.
Kev: admission control sketch (per-tenant):
```yaml
admission_control:
  mode: token_bucket
  refill_per_sec: 10
  burst: 100
  default_rps_cap: 50
  emergency_route: fallback-small-model
```
Kev: token bucket will immediately shed sustained bursts and keep the scheduler sane while warm pool scales.
Cam: can we also route overflow requests to a cheaper/smaller model for non-critical endpoints? e.g., fallback to gpt-small variant to avoid blocking critical flows.
Maria: I'll add a temporary route for non-SLA tenants to fallback-small-model and apply the warm pool change now.
deploy-bot: autoscaler config patch queued: patch/us-west1/warm-pool-increase -> in_progress (rollout id: r-4921) :gear:
ops-bot: alert suppression enabled for alert-group:queue-spike-us-west1 for 20m to reduce noise.
Maria: patch applied: `kubectl apply -f /configs/autoscaler/us-west1-warmpool.yaml` -> success. warm_pool_min=6, scale_up_threshold=65%. watching metrics.
Kev: I'll start a short-lived admission-control feature flag for the token-bucket on canary traffic (10% of tenants) so we can validate without global rollout.
Anya: updating scale_down_grace to 600s on canary too. also increasing controller reconciliation window to avoid tight loops.
Maria: latency dropping — queue depth down ~80% in last 3m, 429s gone for acme-prod. good sign.
Cam: nice. next steps: Kev -> implement per-tenant token-bucket (canary), Anya -> change controller scale-down/reconcile defaults, Maria -> keep warm_pool at 6 for 30m then reassess, Cam -> postmortem + config recommendations.
Kev: will open a PR with tests and config toggle.
Anya: I'll document recommended defaults in infra-runbook.
Cam: thanks all. follow-up sync in #eng-infra in 45m to lock in long-term values. :thumbsup:
